correctness.rationale: An independent set of a clique substitution uses at most one vertex per clique and dominates iff its support is a dominating base set, proving all minimum-set vertices. Token slides split exhaustively into label changes or base slides with common labels fixed, yielding the graph fibers, precise edge counts, components and degrees. Projecting a lifted walk accounts for every persistent mismatched label, while lifting any base walk and setting labels on last entry realizes equality of path lengths. The cyclic 2/3-gap counting independently proves the specializing formulas, with n>=4 boundary. The actual standalone verify.py tests 180 profiles and 1870 directly computed path pairs; all checks passed. Finite checks support, but do not prove, the general statement.

value.rationale: Minimum independent dominating sets are a natural nonhereditary reconfiguration state space. Clique substitution creates exponentially many labelled states while preserving the component partition; the theorem determines every local/cross-fiber adjacency, exact weighted edge and degree census, and all pair distances via a small base-walk optimization rather than simply computing the minimum parameter. This yields general controllable lifts and a closed infinite family of cycle-blowup reconfiguration graphs; the metric and nonuniform data are not implied by the ordinary cycle enumeration alone. The proof requires an explicit persistent-label path argument, not only a textbook independence-number identity.
